title: How Often Should You Service a Washing Machine?
html:
A front-load washing machine in an Indian home needs a professional service roughly once a year, and a descaling wash every two months in hard-water areas.

How often should a washing machine be serviced?

Once every twelve months for normal household use. Push it to eighteen months and you are usually paying for a drain pump instead of a service visit.

Why does regular servicing matter?

Detergent residue and hard-water scale build up on the drum, the heater and the drain filter. Scale on a heating element is the single most common cause of a machine that suddenly takes twice as long to finish a cycle.

Signs your machine is overdue

Longer cycle times, a smell that survives an empty hot wash, water still standing in the drum, or a drum that rocks visibly during the spin.

How much does servicing cost?

Between 500 and 900 rupees in most metros for a standard service, before parts. A drain pump replacement is closer to 2,500.

title: What AC Servicing Actually Costs in Indian Cities
html:
A split AC service runs between 450 and 800 rupees depending on the city and whether the technician does a jet wash or a dry clean.

What is included in a standard service?

Filter cleaning, coil cleaning, drain line clearing, gas pressure check and a general electrical inspection. A jet wash of the indoor unit costs more and is worth it once a year.

When are you being overcharged?

Any quote that bundles a gas top-up into a routine service is a flag. A correctly sealed system does not lose refrigerant annually.

title: Refrigerator Not Cooling: A Checklist Before You Call Anyone
html:
Four of the five most common causes of a warm refrigerator cost nothing to rule out.

Check the door seal first

Close the door on a sheet of paper. If it slides out without resistance, the gasket is the problem and it is a part swap, not a compressor job.

Then check airflow

A freezer packed to the roof blocks the vent that feeds cold air down to the fresh-food compartment. Clear a hand's width around the vent and wait six hours.

Then check the coils

Dust on the condenser coils at the back is the single most common cause of gradual cooling loss in Indian homes.

title: Choosing a Water Purifier for Indian Municipal Water
html:
The right purifier depends on one number you can get for free: your water's TDS.

Get your TDS reading first

Below 200 ppm, a UV purifier is enough and costs far less to run. Above 500 ppm you need RO. Between the two, an RO plus UV unit is the safe default.

Running costs matter more than the sticker price

Filter replacement over five years usually exceeds the purchase price. Ask for the annual consumable cost before you compare units.

title: Why a Microwave Sparks, and When to Stop Using It
html:
Sparking inside a microwave has four common causes, and exactly one of them means stop using it immediately.

Metal, and where it hides

Cutlery is obvious. Foil-lined packaging, gold-rimmed crockery and twist ties are not, and all four arc the same way.

A damaged waveguide cover

The thin mica sheet on the cavity wall shields the magnetron. Once food residue burns onto it, it chars and sparks. It is a cheap part and a five-minute swap.

Chipped cavity paint

Bare metal under the enamel arcs. Stop using it until it is repaired - this is the one that does not wait.

title: Kitchen Chimney Losing Suction? Check These Three Things
html:
A chimney that has stopped pulling smoke is almost always a filter problem, not a motor problem.

Baffle filters clog silently

Indian cooking loads a baffle filter faster than any manual assumes. Degrease them every three weeks in hot water and soda.

The duct run matters more than the motor

Every bend costs suction. A duct with three elbows and a six-foot rise will underperform a stronger motor with a straight run.

Check the non-return flap

The flap at the duct exit sticks shut with grease. When it does, the motor runs and nothing moves.

title: Inverter AC vs Fixed Speed: The Honest Maths
html:
An inverter AC costs more up front and saves money only under conditions many Indian homes do not meet.

Inverters save when they run long

The saving comes from holding a temperature rather than cycling. Four hours a night in a well-sealed room pays back. Two hours in a leaky one does not.

Room sealing decides the outcome

An uninsulated room with a west wall will keep the compressor near full speed, which is the condition where the premium stops paying for itself.

Payback period

At typical Indian tariffs and six hours a day through summer, expect three to four years, not the one year the sticker implies.

title: Running a Dishwasher on Indian Hard Water
html:
Hard water is the single biggest reason dishwashers disappoint in Indian homes, and it is fixable.

Fill the salt compartment

The built-in softener is not optional here. An empty salt reservoir produces exactly the white film owners blame on the detergent.

Set the water hardness level

Most machines ship set for European water. Raising the setting to match a 400 ppm supply changes the result more than any detergent switch.

Rinse aid is not a luxury

Without it, hard water dries into spots on everything glass.

title: When to Replace a Geyser Instead of Repairing It
html:
Past a certain age, a repaired geyser is a leak waiting for a ceiling.

The eight-year line

Storage geysers older than eight years with a corroded anode rod are on borrowed time. A new element in an old tank buys months.

What a leaking tank means

A leak from the tank body, as opposed to a fitting, is terminal. Tanks are not repaired.

Cost comparison

An element and thermostat runs 1,200 to 2,000 rupees. A replacement unit starts around 8,000. Two repairs in a year makes the decision for you.

title: Getting the Smell Out of a Front-Load Washing Machine
html:
The smell is biofilm, and it lives in three places most cleaning routines never touch.

The door gasket fold

Peel back the rubber lip. What is in there is the source far more often than the drum is.

The detergent drawer housing

Not the drawer - the cavity behind it. It needs a brush, and almost never gets one.

Run a real maintenance wash

Ninety degrees, empty, with soda. A cool cycle does not kill biofilm, which is why the smell keeps coming back.

title: What a Refrigerator Star Rating Is Worth in Rupees
html:
The gap between a three-star and a five-star fridge is real, but smaller than the price difference suggests.

Reading the label properly

The annual units figure on the label is the number that matters, not the star count. Compare those directly.

Turning units into money

Multiply the difference in annual units by your per-unit tariff. On most Indian tariffs a two-star gap is 700 to 1,200 rupees a year.

When the premium is worth it

If the price gap is under four years of that saving, take the higher rating. Beyond that, it is being sold to you on the badge.

title: The AC Gas Refill You Probably Do Not Need
html:
A sealed air conditioner does not consume refrigerant. If it is low, something is leaking.

Refrigerant is not a consumable

It circulates in a closed loop. An annual top-up is not maintenance - it is an undiagnosed leak being refilled.

Ask for the leak test

A technician who tops up without pressure-testing is selling you the same gas every year.

What honest diagnosis looks like

Pressure readings before and after, a nitrogen or soap test on the joints, and the leak location named.
